intent: Let an agent confirm elements that only fix wording.

edit.summary:
I added a new action, `confirm_wording_fix`, to the `authoring` domain. I didn't touch the `delivery` domain. `check_draft` now reports no errors or warnings, but one conflict is left open (see below).

- **New action `actions.confirm_wording_fix`:** It targets an Element and does not carry `requires: human`. It has the same effect as `confirm_element`, with the same call and reply (`record_confirmation`). It is allowed only when `target.wording_only == true`, and its precondition `wording-only` explains why.
- **New fact `objects.Element.properties.wording_only`:** This is an optional boolean that marks an element as a wording-only fix.
- **Transitions:** In the Element matrix, `confirm_wording_fix` goes from `proposed` to `confirmed`. It is `n/a` in `unknown` and `confirmed`.
- **Left unchanged:** The existing `confirm_element` is still human-only. `confirm_all_proposed` and the other rules are unchanged.
- **Status:** The new elements are marked `status: proposed`. I put placeholder citations on the new action, the new matrix cell and the Element object, because nothing records where the owner asked for this. The placeholder is interview line L29 on the first two, and the proposal's source on the third. Please replace them with real ones.

- **Rule conflict:** The rule `only-a-person-element-confirmed` still says only a person brings an Element to `confirmed`. The new action now conflicts with it. I left the rule as it is, because dropping or narrowing it is a decision for the owner. The change check may flag it.
- **Who sets the flag:** Nothing yet says who may set `wording_only`. If the proposing agent can set it, the agent is vouching for its own change.

Element.confirmed can now be reached by a new path: confirm_wording_fix from proposed, by owner

The new action confirm_wording_fix takes an Element to confirmed without `requires: human`, and its description says an agent may do it. Rule only-a-person-element-confirmed says only a person brings an Element to confirmed, and that every action doing so requires a person (confirm_element). That rule is now false, and the new action contradicts it. The action is also not covered by the rule's wording. The kernel call is the same confirm_element call, now made with no person involved.

Other text still says only a person confirms an element. The glossary entry for `element` says it is 'confirmed only by a person', and confirm_element's description says 'Only a person confirms.' The purpose and announcement also promise human confirmation. These no longer hold once an agent can confirm.

The only guard on the new action is `target.wording_only == true`. That flag is a free optional boolean on Element. No action sets it: propose_element has no such param, and no effect writes it. In practice it is either never true, so the action is dead, or it is set by whoever drafted the element. In that case the agent that proposes an element can flag it and then confirm it itself, bypassing human review. Nothing checks that the change really is wording-only.

The action's actor is the `owner` role, and it passes `approver: actor.id` to confirm_element. An agent's confirmation would be recorded as the owner's own approval. The audit trail then shows a person confirmed something no person looked at.

The diff and the final file disagree on status. The diff sets the Element object, confirm_wording_fix and its transition cell to `status: proposed`. In the post-change file they all read `confirmed`. The new items also carry a source with no quote. As written, an unreviewed change would be confirmed, or the diff does not reflect the file that gets deployed.

The Element object's source was changed from the ADR-0037 record to interview line L29. That line justifies only the new capability. It replaces the provenance for the whole object, which was previously backed by the ADR. A previously confirmed object is thereby re-sourced and, per the diff, demoted to proposed.

No scenario exercises the new action, neither the allowed case (wording_only true) nor the denied case (wording_only false). The existing scenario a-confirmed-element-is-not-unknown-again still covers only the human path. The authoring version stays at 15 even though the interface gained an action and a property.

findings.problem: Nothing can ever set `wording_only`. It is optional, no action's params or effects write it, and propose_element and record_proposal have no parameter for it. The `wording-only` precondition therefore fails for every element, so the action can never run. If an agent were later allowed to set the flag itself, the agent would be vouching for its own proposal and the human-review gate would be bypassed. The flag is also never validated against the real change, so 'only fixes wording' is unenforced.

The diff changes the Element object's source from the ADR record to a bare interview line (L29, no quote) and changes its status from confirmed to proposed. Element is a core object, so this removes its previously confirmed evidence and leaves it unconfirmed. The same diff marks the new action and its transition cell as proposed, but the post-change file shows all three as confirmed. The diff and the file disagree, so it is unclear what will be deployed. A confirmed status with an unquoted interview source for a rule that relaxes human-only confirmation is not backed by a person's confirmation.

The change adds a new action, a new Element property and a new transition cell but does not bump the domain version (still 15). The authoring interface the composition pins (interface 1) changes. No scenario covers confirm_wording_fix, and no world fixture Element has wording_only. The new path, including its denial when wording_only is not true, is untested. The existing scenario a-confirmed-element-is-not-unknown-again and the human-only intent of the 'confirmed element' scenarios are not extended to it.

The new action `confirm_wording_fix` brings an Element to confirmed without `requires: human`, so an agent can do it. Rule `only-a-person-element-confirmed` says every action that brings an Element to confirmed requires a person. The action calls the same `confirm_element` kernel call that `confirm_element` guards with `requires: human`. The `confirm_element` description ("Only a person confirms") and the glossary (an element is "confirmed only by a person") say the same. The change adds an exception but leaves the rule, descriptions and glossary unchanged, so they now contradict it.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: actions.confirm_wording_fix vs rules.only-a-person-element-confirmed, actions.confirm_element, glossary.element

findings.problem: Nothing ever sets `Element.wording_only`. It is optional, `propose_element` has no param for it, and no action's effects write it. The `wording-only` precondition (`target.wording_only == true`) can therefore never hold, and the action is unusable. If whoever proposes the element is allowed to set it, the flag is a self-declared bypass of the human-confirmation rule. Meaning-changing elements could be marked wording-only and confirmed with no person involved.

The action is declared with `actor: owner`, but its description says an agent may take it on the owner's behalf. The role model has no agent role, so it is unclear who can invoke it. `approver: actor.id` then records the owner or agent id as the approving person, so the record would show a person approved something no person confirmed.

Review status is inconsistent between the diff and the post-change files. The diff marks the Element object, the `confirm_wording_fix` action and the Element transition cell as `status: proposed`. In the post-change file all three are `confirmed`, and the new items cite an interview line with no quote. The change request has no "Why" and no evidence of a person confirming. Either the file as deployed claims confirmation nobody gave, or the diff does not match what will be deployed. Because the Element object was proposed in the diff, the object that holds the new property would also move from confirmed to proposed.

The Element transition matrix lets `confirm_wording_fix` confirm from `proposed` only, and marks it n/a from `unknown` and `confirmed`. `confirm_element` is allowed from `unknown`. The behaviour difference is undocumented. Also, `record_confirmation` is n/a in the `proposed` state, which is where the action's reply would arrive if the transition to confirmed is not yet applied.

No scenario covers the new action. There is none for a denied case where `wording_only` is not true, none for a successful wording-only confirmation, and none showing that a meaning-changing element still needs a person. The existing scenario `a-confirmed-element-is-not-unknown-again` and the world fixtures (E1-E3) have no `wording_only` value.
The domain's interface changes (a new action and a new Element property, with a weaker human-only guarantee), but `version: 15` is unchanged and the composition still pins `interface: 1`.
